notes: Spanish loan. 'Family' itself is just as common in Taglish ('family day', 'family dinner').

examples.tl: Malapit ako sa pamilya ko.
examples.en: I'm close to my family.

examples.tl: May family dinner kami sa Sunday, kaya hindi ako makakasama.
examples.en: We have a family dinner on Sunday, so I can't join.

notes: Usually plural 'mga magulang'. 'Parents' is also fine in Taglish.

examples.tl: Nasa probinsya pa ang mga magulang ko.
examples.en: My parents are still in the province.

examples.tl: Strict ang magulang niya, kaya laging may curfew.
examples.en: Her parents are strict, so there's always a curfew.

notes: Formal or written (forms, prayers: 'Ama Namin'). In speech people say tatay, papa, daddy.

examples.tl: Pangalan ng ama: isulat sa form.
examples.en: Father's name: write it on the form.

examples.tl: Namatay ang ama niya noong bata pa siya.
examples.en: His father died when he was still young.

notes: Address form: 'Tay'. Many Manila families say 'Papa' or 'Daddy'. Old slang: 'erpat'.

examples.tl: Si Tatay ang nagluto ng ulam.
examples.en: Dad was the one who cooked the ulam.

examples.tl: Tay, pahiram ng kotse mamaya.
examples.en: Dad, can I borrow the car later?

notes: Formal or written. In speech: nanay, mama, mommy. 'Ina' also appears in 'Inang Bayan' (motherland).

examples.tl: Pangalan ng ina bago mag-asawa: Reyes.
examples.en: Mother's maiden name: Reyes.

examples.tl: Single mom siya, siya lang ang ina at ama ng mga bata.
examples.en: She's a single mom, both mother and father to the kids.

notes: Address form: 'Nay'. 'Mama'/'Mommy' very common in Manila. Old slang: 'ermat'.

examples.tl: Tumawag si Nanay, kumusta daw ako.
examples.en: Mom called, asking how I am.

examples.tl: Nay, uuwi ako sa Sabado.
examples.en: Mom, I'm coming home on Saturday.

notes: Offspring, not age (compare 'bata' = kid). Also used as address: 'Anak, kain na.'

examples.tl: Ilan ang anak mo?
examples.en: How many kids do you have?

examples.tl: Nag-graduate na ang panganay kong anak.
examples.en: My eldest child already graduated.

notes: Gender-neutral. 'Kapatid na lalaki/babae' when you need the gender; or just kuya/ate/bunso.

examples.tl: Tatlo kaming magkakapatid.
examples.en: There are three of us siblings.

examples.tl: Nasa Dubai ang kapatid ko, OFW.
examples.en: My sibling is in Dubai, an OFW.

notes: Also the default address for any slightly older guy: waiter, Grab driver, guard. See the Kuya/Ate address note.

examples.tl: Si Kuya ang nagbayad ng kuryente.
examples.en: My older brother paid the electric bill.

examples.tl: Close ako sa kuya ko kahit lagi kaming nag-aaway dati.
examples.en: I'm close to my big brother even though we used to fight all the time.

notes: Also address for any slightly older woman (cashier, server). Pronounced AH-teh, two syllables.

examples.tl: Nasa Canada na ang ate ko.
examples.en: My older sister is in Canada now.

examples.tl: Si Ate ang laging nag-aayos ng gulo namin.
examples.en: My big sister is the one who always fixes our mess.

notes: The baby of the family, at any age. 'Spoiled bunso' is a running joke.

examples.tl: Ako ang bunso, kaya ako ang laging inuutusan.
examples.en: I'm the youngest, so I'm always the one sent on errands.

examples.tl: Spoiled talaga ang bunso nila.
examples.en: Their youngest is really spoiled.

notes: Culturally expected to help support younger siblings ('panganay pressure').

examples.tl: Panganay ako, kaya ako ang breadwinner.
examples.en: I'm the eldest, so I'm the breadwinner.

examples.tl: Si panganay ang pinakamatured sa kanila.
examples.en: The eldest is the most mature of them.

notes: Address: 'Lolo' or 'Lo'. Also used for any elderly man, jokingly for friends who act old.

examples.tl: Beterano rin ang lolo ko.
examples.en: My grandfather is also a veteran.

examples.tl: Si Lolo ang nagturo sa akin mag-chess.
examples.en: Grandpa taught me how to play chess.

notes: Address: 'Lola' or 'La'. 'Lola mo!' is a playful retort.

examples.tl: Masarap magluto si Lola.
examples.en: Grandma cooks well.

examples.tl: Dadalawin namin si Lola sa Bulacan ngayong weekend.
examples.en: We're visiting Grandma in Bulacan this weekend.

notes: Also for parents' friends and any man of that generation. 'Tito jokes' = dad jokes.

examples.tl: Si Tito Ben ang nagsundo sa amin sa airport.
examples.en: Uncle Ben picked us up at the airport.

examples.tl: Ang dami niyang tito, ang laki ng pamilya.
examples.en: He has so many uncles, it's a huge family.

notes: Also for mom's friends and your partner's aunts. 'Tita' jokingly = nosy middle-aged-lady energy ('tita questions').

examples.tl: Nakilala ko na ang mga tita ng jowa ko, grabe ang tanong.
examples.en: I met my partner's aunts, wow, the questions.

examples.tl: Tita, salamat po sa pasalubong!
examples.en: Auntie, thank you for the gift!

notes: Cousins are often as close as siblings; 'pinsang buo' = first cousin.

examples.tl: Kasal ng pinsan ko sa Tagaytay next month.
examples.en: My cousin's wedding is in Tagaytay next month.

examples.tl: Magpinsan sila pero parang magkapatid.
examples.en: They're cousins but they're like siblings.

notes: Gender-neutral. Titos and titas are expected to bring pasalubong for pamangkin.

examples.tl: Birthday ng pamangkin ko bukas, bibili ako ng regalo.
examples.en: My niece's birthday is tomorrow, I'll buy a gift.

examples.tl: Ang cute ng pamangkin mo!
examples.en: Your nephew is so cute!

notes: Gender-neutral. 'Mister'/'misis' also common in speech. 'May asawa' = married.

examples.tl: May asawa na ba siya?
examples.en: Is he married already?

examples.tl: Taga-Cebu ang asawa ko.
examples.en: My spouse is from Cebu.

notes: A bit formal/old-fashioned. In Manila speech 'boyfriend', 'BF' or 'jowa' are more common.

examples.tl: May nobyo na si ate, dati pa.
examples.en: Big sister has a boyfriend, for a while now.

examples.tl: Boyfriend mo ba 'yun?
examples.en: Is that your boyfriend?

notes: Same register as nobyo. 'Girlfriend'/'GF' far more common in speech.

examples.tl: Ipakilala mo naman ang nobya mo sa amin.
examples.en: Introduce your girlfriend to us, come on.

examples.tl: Three years na silang mag-GF-BF.
examples.en: They've been girlfriend and boyfriend for three years.

notes: Casual slang, gender-neutral, extremely common. 'May jowa ka na?' = are you seeing someone?

examples.tl: May jowa ka na ba?
examples.en: Do you have a partner now?

examples.tl: Date night namin ng jowa ko sa BGC.
examples.en: My partner and I have date night in BGC.

notes: Formal/literary (songs, forms, news). Rare in speech; people say jowa, boyfriend, girlfriend.

examples.tl: Kasintahan niya ang kasama niya sa litrato.
examples.en: The one with him in the photo is his sweetheart.

notes: 'Friend' is just as common in Taglish. Close friend: 'bestfriend', 'bes', 'beshie'.

examples.tl: Matagal na kaming kaibigan, since college.
examples.en: We've been friends a long time, since college.

examples.tl: Kaibigan ko siya, hindi jowa.
examples.en: He's my friend, not my partner.

notes: Your crew. 'Kabarkada' = a member of your group. 'Barkada trip' = group outing.

examples.tl: Inuman kami ng barkada ko sa Poblacion sa Friday.
examples.en: My friends and I are drinking in Poblacion on Friday.

examples.tl: Kabarkada ko siya noong high school.
examples.en: He was part of my group in high school.

notes: Slang, slightly more 'bro' than barkada. Also address: 'Tropa!' / 'tropz'.

examples.tl: Kasama ko ang tropa sa gym mamaya.
examples.en: I'm with the squad at the gym later.

examples.tl: Tropa, tara, kain tayo!
examples.en: Guys, come on, let's eat!

notes: In condos people also say 'neighbor' or 'katabi namin' (the one next to us).

examples.tl: Maingay ang kapitbahay namin tuwing weekend.
examples.en: Our neighbor is noisy every weekend.

examples.tl: Mabait ang mga kapitbahay sa floor namin.
examples.en: The neighbors on our floor are nice.

notes: Noun and quasi-verb. 'Kasama ko siya' = I'm with him. 'Sama ka?' = coming along? 'Kasama sa bahay' = housemate.

examples.tl: Sino ang kasama mo kagabi?
examples.en: Who were you with last night?

examples.tl: Kasama ba ang jowa mo sa trip?
examples.en: Is your partner coming on the trip?

notes: 'May bisita kami' = we have company. Verb: bumisita/dumalaw = to visit. Guests are always fed.

examples.tl: May bisita kami, kaya nagluto si Mama ng marami.
examples.en: We have guests, so Mom cooked a lot.

examples.tl: Bisita lang ako dito, hindi ako taga-rito.
examples.en: I'm just a visitor here, I'm not from here.

notes: Also a wedding sponsor. Expected to give aguinaldo (cash gift) at Christmas; running joke that ninongs hide in December.

examples.tl: Ninong ako sa binyag ng anak ng kaibigan ko.
examples.en: I'm godfather at my friend's child's baptism.

examples.tl: Nagtatago na ang mga ninong, Pasko na.
examples.en: The godfathers are hiding now, it's Christmas.

notes: Female counterpart of ninong. Being asked to be ninang is an honor (and an expense).

examples.tl: Tinanong ako kung gusto kong maging ninang.
examples.en: I was asked if I'd like to be godmother.

examples.tl: Ninang ko si Tita Marie.
examples.en: Auntie Marie is my godmother.

notes: Your godson/goddaughter. Plural 'mga inaanak'.

examples.tl: Lima ang inaanak ko, mahal ang Pasko.
examples.en: I have five godchildren, Christmas is expensive.

notes: Originally the godfather of your child (or vice versa); now also any close male friend. Female: kumare. Address: 'pare'.

examples.tl: Kumpare ko siya, ninong siya ng anak ko.
examples.en: He's my compadre, he's my kid's godfather.

examples.tl: Mga kumpare ni Tatay ang nag-inuman sa garahe.
examples.en: Dad's buddies were drinking in the garage.

notes: Related: manugang = child-in-law, bayaw = brother-in-law, hipag = sister-in-law. 'In-laws' is common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Mabait ang biyenan ko, swerte ako.
examples.en: My mother-in-law is kind, I'm lucky.

examples.tl: Lunch kami sa mga biyenan ko sa Sunday.
examples.en: We're having lunch at my in-laws' on Sunday.

notes: Gender-neutral. The classic 'biyenan vs manugang' tension is a teleserye staple.

examples.tl: Gusto ng nanay niya ang bagong manugang.
examples.en: His mom likes her new daughter-in-law.

notes: Also address from grandparents: 'Apo, halika.'

examples.tl: Ang dami nang apo ni Lola.
examples.en: Grandma has so many grandchildren now.

examples.tl: Spoiled si bunso kasi favorite na apo.
examples.en: The youngest is spoiled because he's the favorite grandchild.

notes: 'Magkambal' = twins (as a pair). Also a nickname/address between twins.

examples.tl: Kambal sila pero magkaiba ang ugali.
examples.en: They're twins but have different personalities.

notes: Blunt gossip/teleserye register, any gender. Softer: 'ang third party', 'may iba'. Use with care.

examples.tl: Chismis daw, may kabit ang asawa niya.
examples.en: Rumor is her husband has a mistress.

notes: Used exactly as in English, very common. 'Dating jowa' also works.

examples.tl: Nakita ko ang ex ko sa mall, awkward.
examples.en: I saw my ex at the mall, awkward.

examples.tl: Hindi pa siya nakaka-move on sa ex niya.
examples.en: He hasn't moved on from his ex yet.

notes: 'Maraming tao' = crowded. 'Walang tao' = nobody's there. 'Tao po!' = anybody home? (said at a gate).

examples.tl: Ang daming tao sa MRT kanina.
examples.en: There were so many people on the MRT earlier.

examples.tl: Mabait siyang tao.
examples.en: He's a kind person.

notes: Also spelled/said 'lalake'. 'Anak na lalaki' = son. 'Mga lalaki' = the guys.

examples.tl: Sino 'yung lalaking kasama ni ate?
examples.en: Who's that guy with big sister?

examples.tl: Mga lalaki ang nag-asikaso ng ihaw.
examples.en: The guys handled the grilling.

notes: 'Anak na babae' = daughter. 'Mga babae' = the girls/ladies. 'Girl' itself is common in Taglish.

examples.tl: Puro babae ang officemate ko.
examples.en: My officemates are all women.

examples.tl: Ang babaeng 'yun ang bagong manager.
examples.en: That woman is the new manager.

notes: About age (vs anak = offspring). Also adj 'young': 'bata pa siya' = he's still young. 'Mga bata' = the kids.

examples.tl: Maraming bata sa pool tuwing Sabado.
examples.en: There are lots of kids at the pool on Saturdays.

examples.tl: Bata pa siya pero manager na.
examples.en: She's still young but already a manager.

notes: Noun and adj. 'Matanda na' = already old. 'Mas matanda sa akin' = older than me. Polite: 'nakatatanda'.

examples.tl: Mas matanda siya sa akin ng tatlong taon.
examples.en: He's three years older than me.

examples.tl: Pauupo mo ang matanda sa jeep.
examples.en: Let the elderly person sit on the jeep.

notes: Unmarried young man. 'Binata na siya' = he's grown up now. Titas love asking 'binata pa?' (still single?).

examples.tl: Binata pa ba ang kuya mo?
examples.en: Is your older brother still single?

examples.tl: Ang laki na ng pamangkin ko, binata na.
examples.en: My nephew is so grown up now, a young man already.

notes: Counterpart of binata. 'Dalaga na' = she's grown up. 'Dalagang Pilipina' is a cultural ideal/song.

examples.tl: Dalaga na ang anak ni Tita, college na.
examples.en: Auntie's daughter is a young woman now, in college already.

examples.tl: Dalaga pa siya, walang jowa.
examples.en: She's still single, no partner.

notes: Formal: 'Ginoong Santos' (G.) = Mr. Santos. 'Mga ginoo at binibini' = ladies and gentlemen. In speech people say 'sir'.

examples.tl: Ginoong Cruz, puwede po kayong pumasok.
examples.en: Mr. Cruz, you may come in.

notes: Formal: 'Ginang Reyes' (Gng.). Miss = 'Binibini' (Bb.). In speech: 'ma'am', 'misis'.

examples.tl: Para kay Ginang Reyes ang sulat.
examples.en: The letter is for Mrs. Reyes.

en: polite address to customers or strangers
notes: Default polite address by guards, cashiers, Grab drivers, in offices. 'Mamser' jokingly merges both. Reply politely with 'po'.

examples.tl: Sir, bawal po ang shorts dito.
examples.en: Sir, shorts aren't allowed here.

examples.tl: Ma'am, GCash po ba o cash?
examples.en: Ma'am, GCash or cash?

notes: Your actual boss, AND a friendly address to strangers: vendors, tricycle drivers, guards. 'Bossing' is the jokey version.

examples.tl: Boss, magkano 'to?
examples.en: Boss, how much is this?

examples.tl: Masungit ang boss ko sa office.
examples.en: My boss at the office is grumpy.

notes: From kumpare. Men to men, very common. Shortened 'pre'. Similar: 'tol', 'bro', 'tsong', 'dude'.

examples.tl: Pare, tara, inom tayo mamaya.
examples.en: Bro, come on, let's drink later.

examples.tl: Pre, nasaan ka na? Late ka na.
examples.en: Dude, where are you? You're late.

notes: Used as in English, also 'brad' / 'bruh'. Women friends: 'sis', 'bes', 'girl', 'mars'.

examples.tl: Bro, salamat sa libre ha.
examples.en: Bro, thanks for the treat, okay.

examples.tl: Sis, kita tayo sa Glorietta.
examples.en: Sis, let's meet at Glorietta.

en: address for staff or slightly older strangers
notes: Polite-friendly for waiters, drivers, cashiers, guards, vendors, roughly your age or older. Add 'po'. Never rude.

examples.tl: Kuya, para po sa tabi.
examples.en: Kuya, please stop at the side (getting off a jeep).

examples.tl: Ate, isang iced coffee po, less sugar.
examples.en: Ate, one iced coffee please, less sugar.

notes: For noticeably older working men: tricycle driver, guard, vendor, plumber. Respectful, not rude. Female: manang.

examples.tl: Manong, sa 7-Eleven lang po.
examples.en: Manong, just to the 7-Eleven please.

examples.tl: Si Manong guard ang tumanggap ng package.
examples.en: Manong the guard received the package.

notes: For older working women (vendors, helpers). Also adj 'manang' = old-fashioned/prudish in dress or attitude.

examples.tl: Manang, pabili po ng dalawang itlog.
examples.en: Manang, two eggs please.

examples.tl: Manang ang damit niya, parang pang-simba.
examples.en: Her outfit is so old-fashioned, like church clothes.

notes: Calling an elderly vendor or stranger 'Nay' or 'Tay' (from nanay/tatay) is warm and respectful. Also 'Nanay'/'Tatay' in full.

examples.tl: Nay, magkano po ang saging?
examples.en: Ma'am, how much are the bananas?

examples.tl: Tay, dito lang po ako bababa.
examples.en: Sir, I'll get off right here.

notes: Add to anything said to elders, strangers, staff: 'Salamat po.' Variant 'ho'. Dropping it with elders sounds rude; with close friends it sounds jokey.

examples.tl: Magkano po ito?
examples.en: How much is this, please?

examples.tl: Hindi po ako taga-rito.
examples.en: I'm not from here (polite).

notes: Polite yes to elders/strangers; 'oo' is plain yes among peers. 'Hindi po' = polite no.

examples.tl: Opo, kumain na po ako.
examples.en: Yes, I've already eaten.

examples.tl: Opo, Tita, uuwi ako sa Pasko.
examples.en: Yes, Auntie, I'll come home for Christmas.

notes: 'Officemate' and 'workmate' are more common in Manila offices than katrabaho.

examples.tl: Katrabaho ko siya dati sa BPO.
examples.en: He was my coworker before at the BPO.

examples.tl: Lunch out kami ng mga officemate ko.
examples.en: I'm having lunch out with my officemates.

notes: Also 'schoolmate', 'batchmate' (same graduating year), 'kabatch'.

examples.tl: Kaklase ko siya noong high school.
examples.en: She was my classmate in high school.

examples.tl: Reunion ng mga kaklase ko sa December.
examples.en: My classmates' reunion is in December.

notes: Someone you know but not a friend. 'Kakilala ko lang siya' = I just know him.

examples.tl: Hindi kami close, kakilala ko lang siya.
examples.en: We're not close, he's just an acquaintance.

examples.tl: May kakilala ako sa BIR, tanungin ko.
examples.en: I know someone at the BIR, I'll ask.

notes: The polite, legal term ('Kasambahay Law'). 'Katulong' is older and now avoided. Address them as Ate/Kuya or by name.

examples.tl: Day off ng kasambahay namin tuwing Linggo.
examples.en: Our house helper's day off is every Sunday.

examples.tl: Naghahanap sila ng stay-in na kasambahay.
examples.en: They're looking for a live-in helper.

notes: Live-in or daytime nanny, very common in middle-class Manila households. Address: 'Yaya' or 'Ate'.

examples.tl: Umalis ang yaya nila, kaya WFH si misis.
examples.en: Their nanny quit, so the wife is working from home.

examples.tl: Mahal na ang sweldo ng yaya sa Makati.
examples.en: Nanny salaries are expensive in Makati now.

notes: Everywhere: malls, condos, banks. Address: 'Kuya guard', 'Manong', 'Sir'. They'll ask 'Saan po kayo?' (where to?).

examples.tl: Iwan mo lang sa guard ang package.
examples.en: Just leave the package with the guard.

examples.tl: Tinanong ako ng guard kung saan ako pupunta.
examples.en: The guard asked me where I was going.

notes: 60+. Senior ID gives 20% discount; 'senior lane' at banks and pharmacies. 'Senior na si Tatay.'

examples.tl: May senior discount po ba kayo?
examples.en: Do you have a senior discount?

examples.tl: Pumila si Lola sa senior lane.
examples.en: Grandma lined up in the senior lane.

notes: Collective. 'Mga kabataan ngayon' = kids these days (classic tito line). Also 'kabataan' = youth (time of life).

examples.tl: Puro cellphone ang mga kabataan ngayon.
examples.en: Young people today are all on their phones.

notes: Plural: 'sinu-sino'. 'Sino 'yan?' = who's that? (phone/door). 'Kanino' = whose/to whom.

examples.tl: Sino 'yan? Kilala mo?
examples.en: Who's that? Do you know them?

examples.tl: Sinu-sino ang kasama mo sa Baguio?
examples.en: Who all are you with in Baguio?

notes: Also 'fun' for events: 'masaya ang party'. 'Saya' = joy; 'nasiyahan' = enjoyed (formal).

examples.tl: Masaya ako para sa inyo!
examples.en: I'm happy for you guys!

examples.tl: Masaya ang team building namin sa Batangas.
examples.en: Our team building in Batangas was fun.

notes: 'Nalulungkot ako' = I'm feeling sad. 'Lungkot' = sadness. Taglish 'sad' is very common too.

examples.tl: Malungkot siya kasi umalis ang kaibigan niya papuntang Canada.
examples.en: She's sad because her friend left for Canada.

examples.tl: Nalulungkot ako kapag Pasko na wala akong kasama.
examples.en: I get sad at Christmas when I have no one with me.

notes: Used as-is: 'Sad ako', 'nakaka-sad', 'na-sad ako'. Lighter than malungkot.

examples.tl: Sad ako, cancelled ang trip namin.
examples.en: I'm sad, our trip got cancelled.

examples.tl: Nakaka-sad 'yung balita tungkol sa lolo niya.
examples.en: The news about his grandfather is saddening.

notes: 'Galit ka ba sa akin?' = are you mad at me? 'Nagalit' = got angry; 'nagagalit' = is getting angry.

examples.tl: Galit si Mama kasi late ako umuwi.
examples.en: Mom's angry because I came home late.

examples.tl: Huwag ka nang magalit, nag-sorry na ako.
examples.en: Don't be angry anymore, I already said sorry.

notes: Incompleted aspect of magalit. 'Nagalit' = got angry (done). 'Magagalit' = will get angry.

examples.tl: Nagagalit si boss kapag late ang report.
examples.en: The boss gets angry when the report is late.

examples.tl: Magagalit ang jowa ko kung makalimutan ko ang monthsary.
examples.en: My partner will get mad if I forget our monthsary.

notes: 'Takot ako sa ipis' = I'm scared of cockroaches. 'Natatakot' = feeling afraid (now). 'Nakakatakot' = scary.

examples.tl: Takot siya sa aso.
examples.en: She's afraid of dogs.

examples.tl: Takot akong mag-drive sa EDSA.
examples.en: I'm scared to drive on EDSA.

notes: From matakot. 'Natakot ako' = I got scared. 'Natatakot ako na...' = I'm afraid that...

examples.tl: Natatakot akong mag-isa sa condo kapag may bagyo.
examples.en: I'm scared being alone in the condo when there's a typhoon.

examples.tl: Natakot ako sa lindol kanina.
examples.en: The earthquake earlier scared me.

notes: From kaba (nervousness). 'Kinabahan ako' = I got nervous. Texting: 'kinakabahan ako huhu'.

examples.tl: Kinakabahan ako sa interview ko bukas.
examples.en: I'm nervous about my interview tomorrow.

examples.tl: Kinabahan ako nang makilala ko ang parents niya.
examples.en: I got nervous when I met her parents.

notes: Used as-is: 'Excited ako', 'na-excite ako', 'nakaka-excite'. Tagalog 'nasasabik' is formal.

examples.tl: Excited na ako sa trip natin sa Palawan!
examples.en: I'm excited for our Palawan trip!

examples.tl: Na-excite ang mga bata sa bagong puppy.
examples.en: The kids got excited about the new puppy.

notes: 'Inis ako sa kanya' = I'm annoyed at him. 'Nakakainis' = annoying. 'Naiinis' = getting annoyed.

examples.tl: Inis ako kasi laging late ang Grab.
examples.en: I'm annoyed because the Grab is always late.

examples.tl: Inis na inis siya sa kapitbahay namin.
examples.en: She's super annoyed at our neighbor.

notes: From mainis. 'Nainis ako' = I got annoyed. Super common in GC rants.

examples.tl: Naiinis ako sa traffic sa EDSA araw-araw.
examples.en: I get annoyed with the EDSA traffic every day.

examples.tl: Nainis siya kasi hindi ako nag-reply.
examples.en: She got annoyed because I didn't reply.

notes: From hiya (shame/shyness), a core Filipino concept. 'Nahiya ako' = I was embarrassed. 'Nakakahiya' = embarrassing.

examples.tl: Nahihiya akong humingi ng tulong sa kanila.
examples.en: I'm shy about asking them for help.

examples.tl: Nahiya ako, nakalimutan ko ang pangalan niya.
examples.en: I was embarrassed, I forgot her name.

notes: Also 'Nakakahiya naman' when someone gives you something = oh, you shouldn't have. Slang: 'nakakahiya', 'shems'.

examples.tl: Nakakahiya, nadapa ako sa harap ng crush ko.
examples.en: So embarrassing, I tripped in front of my crush.

examples.tl: Nakakahiya naman, ikaw na naman ang nag-libre.
examples.en: Oh you shouldn't have, you treated us again.

notes: 'Stress ako' / 'na-stress ako' / 'nakaka-stress'. Also 'stressed' as-is.

examples.tl: Na-stress ako sa trabaho buong linggo.
examples.en: I was stressed from work all week.

examples.tl: Nakaka-stress ang pag-renew ng visa.
examples.en: Renewing the visa is stressful.

notes: 'Pagod ako' = I'm tired. 'Napagod' = got tired. 'Nakakapagod' = tiring. Slang: 'pagod na pagod', 'tired na'.

examples.tl: Pagod ako galing sa gym.
examples.en: I'm tired from the gym.

examples.tl: Pagod na pagod si Mama pagkatapos ng handaan.
examples.en: Mom was exhausted after the party.

notes: Nakaka- + root = 'causes X'. Common with people too: 'nakakapagod kausap' = tiring to talk to.

examples.tl: Nakakapagod ang commute mula Cavite hanggang Makati.
examples.en: The commute from Cavite to Makati is exhausting.

examples.tl: Nakakapagod siyang kausap, puro reklamo.
examples.en: He's tiring to talk to, all complaints.

notes: 'Bored ako' / 'nabo-bored ako' / 'nakaka-bored'. Tagalog: 'naiinip' (impatient/bored waiting).

examples.tl: Bored ako, walang magawa sa condo.
examples.en: I'm bored, nothing to do in the condo.

examples.tl: Nabo-bored ang mga bata sa misa.
examples.en: The kids get bored at mass.

notes: From inip. Specifically the boredom of waiting. 'Nainip ako' = I got tired of waiting.

examples.tl: Naiinip na ako, isang oras na akong naghihintay sa Grab.
examples.en: I'm getting impatient, I've been waiting an hour for the Grab.

examples.tl: Nainip ang mga bisita, late ang celebrant.
examples.en: The guests got restless, the celebrant was late.

notes: Taglish verb: 'Na-miss kita', 'na-miss ko ang adobo ni Lola'. 'Nami-miss' = currently missing. Tagalog 'nangungulila' is formal.

examples.tl: Na-miss kita! Ang tagal nating hindi nagkita.
examples.en: I missed you! It's been so long since we saw each other.

examples.tl: Nami-miss ko na ang pamilya ko sa probinsya.
examples.en: I'm missing my family in the province.

notes: Everyday text to partner/family. 'Miss ko na kayo' to a group. 'Miss kita' alone also works.

examples.tl: Miss na kita, kailan ka uuwi?
examples.en: I miss you already, when are you coming home?

examples.tl: Miss ko na kayo, tropa. Inuman soon!
examples.en: I miss you guys, squad. Drinks soon!

notes: Taglish nakaka- form. Said when something brings back fond memories: old photos, a reunion, hometown food.

examples.tl: Nakakamiss ang college days natin.
examples.en: Our college days make me miss them.

examples.tl: Nakakamiss 'yung tambay natin sa kanto dati.
examples.en: I miss how we used to hang out at the corner.

notes: Also 'expensive'. 'Mahal' as address = dear/babe. 'Mahal kita' = I love you. 'Mahal ko siya' = I love him/her.

examples.tl: Mahal, nasaan ka na?
examples.en: Babe, where are you now?

examples.tl: Mahal niya talaga ang pamilya niya.
examples.en: He really loves his family.

notes: Romantic or family. 'Mahal ko kayo' to parents/kids. 'Love you' / 'lab yu' also common in text.

examples.tl: Mahal kita, ingat ka sa biyahe.
examples.en: I love you, take care on the trip.

examples.tl: Mahal ko kayo, Ma, Pa. Happy anniversary!
examples.en: I love you, Mom, Dad. Happy anniversary!

notes: Object-focus verb: minahal (loved), minamahal (loves), mamahalin (will love). 'Minamahal kong asawa' = my beloved spouse.

examples.tl: Mahalin mo ang sarili mo muna.
examples.en: Love yourself first.

examples.tl: Minahal ko siya pero hindi kami para sa isa't isa.
examples.en: I loved her but we weren't meant for each other.

notes: 'Gusto ko siya' = I like him/her (can be romantic). 'Gusto kita' is a confession. Also 'gusto ko ng kape' = I want coffee.

examples.tl: Gusto ko ang mga kaibigan mo, mababait sila.
examples.en: I like your friends, they're nice.

examples.tl: Gusto mo bang sumama sa amin sa Tagaytay?
examples.en: Do you want to come with us to Tagaytay?

notes: A confession, lighter than 'Mahal kita'. 'May gusto ako sa 'yo' = I have feelings for you. 'Type kita' = I'm into you.

examples.tl: Gusto kita. Puwede ba kitang ligawan?
examples.en: I like you. Can I court you?

examples.tl: Umamin siya: may gusto raw siya sa akin.
examples.en: He confessed: he said he has feelings for me.

notes: Opposite of gusto. 'Ayaw ko' = I don't want to. 'Ayaw niya sa akin' = she doesn't like me. 'Ayoko' = ayaw ko (spoken).

examples.tl: Ayaw ng tatay niya sa akin.
examples.en: Her dad doesn't like me.

examples.tl: Ayoko nang makipag-usap sa kanya.
examples.en: I don't want to talk to him anymore.

notes: 'Nagseselos' = is jealous (now). 'Nagselos' = got jealous. 'Seloso/selosa' = jealous type. 'Inggit' = envy (of things).

examples.tl: Nagseselos ang jowa ko sa officemate ko.
examples.en: My partner is jealous of my officemate.

examples.tl: Selos lang 'yun, hindi galit.
examples.en: That's just jealousy, not anger.

notes: Used as-is: 'Proud ako sa 'yo'. 'Ipinagmamalaki' is formal. Compare 'mayabang' = arrogant (negative).

examples.tl: Proud ako sa 'yo, anak.
examples.en: I'm proud of you, my child.

examples.tl: Proud parents sila sa graduation.
examples.en: They were proud parents at the graduation.

notes: From mag-alala. 'Nag-alala ako' = I got worried. 'Huwag kang mag-alala' = don't worry. Text: 'worried ako'.

examples.tl: Nag-aalala si Mama kasi hindi ako nag-text.
examples.en: Mom is worried because I didn't text.

examples.tl: Huwag kang mag-alala, okay lang ako.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'm fine.

notes: The all-purpose 'fine'. 'Okay lang ako' = I'm okay. 'Okay lang ba?' = is it okay? Also 'ayos lang'. Sometimes hides tampo.

examples.tl: Okay lang, hindi ko na kailangan.
examples.en: It's fine, I don't need it anymore.

examples.tl: Okay lang ako, pagod lang.
examples.en: I'm fine, just tired.

notes: From kilig, the untranslatable romantic thrill. 'Nakakakilig' = so sweet it gives you butterflies. 'Kinikilig' = currently giddy.

examples.tl: Kinilig ako nang hawakan niya ang kamay ko.
examples.en: I got butterflies when he held my hand.

examples.tl: Kinikilig si ate sa text ng crush niya.
examples.en: Big sister is giddy over her crush's text.

notes: 'Nakakatawa siya' = he's funny. Text: 'HAHAHA nakakatawa'. 'Natawa ako' = I laughed.

examples.tl: Nakakatawa ang mga tito jokes niya.
examples.en: His dad jokes are funny.

examples.tl: Natawa ako sa meme na sinend mo sa GC.
examples.en: I laughed at the meme you sent to the group chat.

notes: About people or situations. Slang short form: 'nakakaloka', 'nakaka-badtrip'.

examples.tl: Nakakainis, cancelled ulit ang booking ko.
examples.en: So annoying, my booking got cancelled again.

examples.tl: Nakakainis siya kausap kapag lasing.
examples.en: He's annoying to talk to when drunk.

notes: 'Nakakatakot sa Quiapo kapag gabi' = Quiapo is scary at night. Also 'creepy'.

examples.tl: Nakakatakot ang balita tungkol sa bagyo.
examples.en: The news about the typhoon is scary.

examples.tl: Nakakatakot maglakad diyan kapag madilim.
examples.en: It's scary to walk there when it's dark.

notes: From loka (crazy). Originally gay lingo, now mainstream. Reaction to anything shocking, good or bad.

examples.tl: Nakakaloka, 500 pesos ang isang kape!
examples.en: Insane, one coffee is 500 pesos!

examples.tl: Nakakaloka ang chismis sa GC namin.
examples.en: The gossip in our group chat is wild.

notes: From gulat. 'Gulat ako' = I'm surprised. 'Nakakagulat' = surprising. 'Surprise party' is 'surprise' as-is.

examples.tl: Nagulat ako nang bumisita ang pinsan ko galing Dubai.
examples.en: I was surprised when my cousin visited from Dubai.

examples.tl: Nagulat siya sa surprise party niya.
examples.en: She was surprised at her surprise party.

notes: Untranslatable: withdrawing quietly because someone let you down, expecting them to make it up. 'Nagtatampo' = is sulking. 'Suyuin' = to coax out of tampo.

examples.tl: Nagtatampo si Lola kasi hindi kami dumalaw sa birthday niya.
examples.en: Grandma is sulking because we didn't visit on her birthday.

examples.tl: May tampo pa siya sa akin, kaya hindi nag-reply.
examples.en: She's still hurt at me, so she isn't replying.

notes: Physical or emotional. 'Nasaktan ako sa sinabi mo' = what you said hurt me. 'Masakit' = painful.

examples.tl: Nasaktan siya sa sinabi ng ate niya.
examples.en: She was hurt by what her sister said.

examples.tl: Nasaktan ako noong nag-break kami.
examples.en: I got hurt when we broke up.

notes: Taglish; mostly about exes and love life. 'Bitter ka lang' = you're just bitter. Also 'bitter sa love'.

examples.tl: Bitter pa siya sa ex niya kaya ayaw niyang mag-date.
examples.en: He's still bitter about his ex so he doesn't want to date.

examples.tl: Bitter ka lang kasi walang ka-date sa Valentine's.
examples.en: You're just bitter because you have no date on Valentine's.

notes: 'Badtrip ako' = I'm in a bad mood. 'Nakaka-badtrip' = what a bummer. 'Na-badtrip ako sa kanya' = he put me off.

examples.tl: Badtrip, na-late ako kasi baha sa Taft.
examples.en: Ugh, I was late because Taft was flooded.

examples.tl: Na-badtrip ako sa waiter, ang sungit.
examples.en: The waiter put me in a bad mood, so grumpy.

notes: Gana = appetite/drive. 'Wala akong gana' = I'm not feeling it. 'Nawalan ako ng gana' = I lost interest.

examples.tl: Wala akong gana kumain, broken-hearted.
examples.en: I have no appetite, I'm broken-hearted.

examples.tl: Walang gana mag-work si bes, Monday.
examples.en: Bestie has no drive to work, it's Monday.

notes: Taglish verb from enjoy. 'Mag-enjoy ka!' = have fun! 'Nag-e-enjoy' = is enjoying. Tagalog 'nasiyahan' is formal.

examples.tl: Nag-enjoy ba kayo sa Boracay?
examples.en: Did you guys have fun in Boracay?

examples.tl: Mag-enjoy kayo sa date, ingat!
examples.en: Enjoy your date, take care!

notes: From 'paranoid'. 'Napapraning ako' = I'm getting paranoid. Common for overthinking a text that got seen-zoned.

examples.tl: Napapraning ako, hindi pa siya nag-reply since kahapon.
examples.en: I'm getting paranoid, she hasn't replied since yesterday.

examples.tl: Praning siya sa mga chismis sa office.
examples.en: He's paranoid about the office gossip.

notes: From hypertension. 'Na-high blood ako' = I got worked up. 'Nakaka-high blood' = infuriating. Jokey tone.

examples.tl: Na-high blood si Tatay sa bill ng Meralco.
examples.en: Dad got worked up over the Meralco bill.

examples.tl: Nakaka-high blood ang customer service nila.
examples.en: Their customer service is infuriating.

notes: The #1 compliment for a person. 'Mabait siya' = he's nice. Plural: 'mababait'. Root bait = goodness.

examples.tl: Mabait ang mga magulang ng jowa ko, swerte ako.
examples.en: My partner's parents are kind, I'm lucky.

examples.tl: Mabait ang driver, hindi nag-reklamo sa traffic.
examples.en: The driver was nice, didn't complain about the traffic.

notes: Opposite of mabait. 'Sungit' = grumpiness. 'Nagsusungit' = being grumpy right now. Common for staff reviews.

examples.tl: Masungit ang cashier sa 7-Eleven kanina.
examples.en: The cashier at the 7-Eleven earlier was grumpy.

examples.tl: Masungit si boss kapag Monday.
examples.en: The boss is cranky on Mondays.

notes: Root arte (acting). Fussy about food, clothes, cleanliness, or overly dramatic. Mild tease among friends.

examples.tl: Maarte siya sa pagkain, ayaw ng street food.
examples.en: She's fussy with food, won't eat street food.

examples.tl: Huwag kang maarte, sakay na sa jeep.
examples.en: Don't be fussy, just get on the jeep.

notes: For people and places. 'Tahimik lang siya' = he's the quiet type. 'Tumahimik ka' = be quiet.

examples.tl: Tahimik siya sa GC pero madaldal in person.
examples.en: She's quiet in the group chat but talkative in person.

examples.tl: Tahimik ang condo namin, walang maingay na kapitbahay.
examples.en: Our condo is quiet, no noisy neighbors.

notes: Root daldal (chatter). Friendly tease. 'Ang daldal mo!' = you talk so much.

examples.tl: Madaldal ang tita niya, hindi ako nakapagsalita.
examples.en: Her aunt is so talkative, I couldn't get a word in.

examples.tl: Madaldal ang Grab driver ko, kuwento tungkol sa politika.
examples.en: My Grab driver was chatty, stories about politics.

notes: Root talino. Plural: 'matatalino'. 'Matalino ka' is a sincere compliment; 'ang talino!' = so smart!

examples.tl: Matalino ang pamangkin ko, laging top sa klase.
examples.en: My niece is smart, always top of the class.

examples.tl: Matalino siya pero tamad mag-aral.
examples.en: He's smart but lazy about studying.

notes: Harsh when aimed at someone; among close friends it's playful ('Tanga mo! HAHAHA'). Also self-directed: 'tanga ako sa love'. Avoid with strangers.

examples.tl: Ang tanga ko, naiwan ko ang wallet ko sa Grab.
examples.en: I'm so dumb, I left my wallet in the Grab.

examples.tl: Tanga ka ba? Niloko ka na niya nang dalawang beses.
examples.en: Are you stupid? He's cheated on you twice already.

notes: 'Tinatamad ako' = I feel lazy / can't be bothered (very common). 'Katamaran' = laziness.

examples.tl: Tinatamad akong lumabas, uulan daw.
examples.en: I don't feel like going out, it's going to rain.

examples.tl: Tamad ang kapatid ko, hindi tumutulong sa bahay.
examples.en: My brother is lazy, doesn't help around the house.

notes: Root sipag. Classic praise for OFWs, students, employees. 'Ang sipag mo!' = you're so hardworking.

examples.tl: Masipag ang mga Pilipino sa abroad.
examples.en: Filipinos abroad are hardworking.

examples.tl: Masipag ang kasambahay namin, maaga pa lang tapos na.
examples.en: Our helper is diligent, done early in the day.

notes: Root yabang. 'Nagyayabang' = showing off. 'Yabang mo!' = you're so cocky. A serious social sin in PH culture.

examples.tl: Mayabang ang bagong officemate, puro kuwento ng achievements.
examples.en: The new officemate is arrogant, all stories about his achievements.

examples.tl: Huwag kang magyabang sa social media.
examples.en: Don't show off on social media.

notes: Personality trait (vs 'nahihiya' = feeling shy right now). Root hiya.

examples.tl: Mahiyain ang anak nila, nagtatago sa likod ng mama.
examples.en: Their kid is shy, hiding behind her mom.

examples.tl: Mahiyain ako dati, pero na-train ako sa sales.
examples.en: I was shy before, but sales trained me out of it.

notes: Pala- + kaibigan = tends to make friends. 'Friendly' as-is is also common.

examples.tl: Palakaibigan siya, kaya ang dami niyang kilala sa Makati.
examples.en: He's outgoing, so he knows tons of people in Makati.

examples.tl: Palakaibigan ang mga Pilipino sa mga foreigner.
examples.en: Filipinos are friendly toward foreigners.

notes: Root alaga (to care for). High praise for a partner or parent. 'Alagang-alaga' = well taken care of.

examples.tl: Maalaga ang jowa ko, laging may baon akong tubig.
examples.en: My partner is caring, I always have water packed.

examples.tl: Maalaga si Ate sa mga pamangkin niya.
examples.en: Big sister is attentive to her nieces and nephews.

notes: Root tapang. Also 'strong' for coffee ('matapang na kape'). 'Lakas ng loob' = courage.

examples.tl: Matapang si Lolo noong giyera.
examples.en: Grandpa was brave during the war.

examples.tl: Matapang siya, nag-resign nang walang backup job.
examples.en: She's bold, resigned without a backup job.

notes: Insulting but also teasing: 'Duwag ka!' when a friend won't ride the roller coaster. 'Takot' is the feeling; duwag is the label.

examples.tl: Duwag siya, hindi siya umamin sa crush niya.
examples.en: He's a coward, he never confessed to his crush.

notes: Also 'good' for things ('magandang balita'). For women; men are gwapo. 'Ganda' = beauty. 'Ang ganda mo!' = you look great.

examples.tl: Ang ganda ng ate mo!
examples.en: Your sister is so pretty!

examples.tl: Maganda ang kapatid niya, model.
examples.en: His sister is beautiful, a model.

notes: Spanish loan. 'Gwaping' is jokey. 'Pogi' is the casual synonym ('ang pogi!'). 'Gwapa' for women is Bisaya, not Tagalog.

examples.tl: Gwapo ang bago nilang manager.
examples.en: Their new manager is handsome.

examples.tl: Pogi ang jowa ni Ate, parang artista.
examples.en: Big sister's boyfriend is handsome, like an actor.

notes: As in English, for babies, pets, crushes. 'Ang cute!' 'Cute siya' can also mean 'he's a bit attractive'.

examples.tl: Ang cute ng baby ng pinsan ko!
examples.en: My cousin's baby is so cute!

examples.tl: Cute 'yung barista sa coffee shop sa Salcedo.
examples.en: The barista at the Salcedo coffee shop is cute.

notes: For people. 'Mataas' = tall/high for things. 'Tangkad' = height. Common first observation about foreigners.

examples.tl: Matangkad ang tatay niya, basketball player dati.
examples.en: Her dad is tall, a basketball player before.

examples.tl: Ang tangkad mo! Ilang feet ka?
examples.en: You're so tall! How many feet are you?

notes: General 'small'. For height, 'pandak' = short (blunt, teasing). 'Maliit lang siya pero matapang.'

examples.tl: Maliit si Lola pero malakas pa.
examples.en: Grandma is small but still strong.

examples.tl: Maliit lang ang condo namin, studio type.
examples.en: Our condo is just small, studio type.

notes: Said more openly than in the US (relatives will comment: 'tumaba ka!' = you gained weight). Softer: 'chubby', 'malusog' (healthy).

examples.tl: Tumaba ka! Masarap siguro ang buhay sa Makati.
examples.en: You gained weight! Life in Makati must be good.

examples.tl: Mataba ang pusa nila, spoiled.
examples.en: Their cat is fat, spoiled.

notes: 'Pumayat ka' = you lost weight (compliment or concern). 'Slim' / 'sexy' for the flattering version.

examples.tl: Pumayat ka, nag-gym ka ba?
examples.en: You lost weight, have you been going to the gym?

examples.tl: Payat siya noong high school, ngayon jacked na.
examples.en: He was skinny in high school, now he's jacked.

notes: Root puti (white). Often meant as a compliment in PH, which can feel odd to Americans. 'Pumuti ka' = you got lighter.

examples.tl: Maputi ang nanay niya, half-Spanish.
examples.en: Her mom is fair-skinned, half-Spanish.

examples.tl: Maputi ka kasi laging aircon.
examples.en: You're pale because you're always in the aircon.

notes: Root itim (black). Can be blunt; 'morena/moreno' or 'kayumanggi' are the flattering words. 'Umitim ka' = you got tan (after a beach trip).

examples.tl: Umitim ako sa Boracay, sunog.
examples.en: I got dark in Boracay, sunburned.

examples.tl: Maitim siya pero maganda ang kutis.
examples.en: She's dark-skinned but has beautiful skin.

notes: Morena (f) / moreno (m). The complimentary word for brown skin, 'morena beauty'. Kayumanggi = brown (formal).

examples.tl: Morena ang jowa ko, ayaw niya ng whitening.
examples.en: My partner is morena, she won't use whitening.

examples.tl: Moreno siya, laging nasa beach.
examples.en: He's tan, always at the beach.

notes: Suplado (m) / suplada (f). Someone who seems too cool to talk to you. Very common label.

examples.tl: Suplada ang bagong neighbor, hindi bumabati.
examples.en: The new neighbor is snobbish, doesn't say hi.

examples.tl: Suplado siya sa una pero mabait pala.
examples.en: He seemed aloof at first but turned out nice.

notes: Root lambing (affection/sweet-talk). 'Naglalambing' = being affectionate / sweet-talking to get something.

examples.tl: Malambing ang anak nila, laging nakayakap.
examples.en: Their kid is affectionate, always hugging.

examples.tl: Naglalambing si ate kay Papa kasi may hihingin.
examples.en: Big sister is sweet-talking Dad because she wants something.

notes: Root kulit. Kids who won't stop, friends who keep nagging. 'Ang kulit mo!' Also 'kulit' = horsing around.

examples.tl: Makulit ang pamangkin ko, hindi natatahimik.
examples.en: My nephew is pesky, never settles down.

examples.tl: Ang kulit mo, sinabi ko nang hindi ako puwede.
examples.en: You're so persistent, I already said I can't.

notes: Someone who ignores rules or warnings. Used for kids, friends, and rule-breaking citizens ('mga pasaway').

examples.tl: Pasaway ang kuya ko noong bata, laging napapagalitan.
examples.en: My brother was a troublemaker as a kid, always getting scolded.

examples.tl: Pasaway ang mga driver dito, hindi sumusunod sa lane.
examples.en: Drivers here are rule-breakers, they don't stay in lane.

notes: Teasing or critical. Opposite: 'galante' (generous). 'Matipid' = thrifty (positive).

examples.tl: Kuripot si kuya, hindi nag-libre sa birthday niya.
examples.en: My brother is stingy, didn't treat us on his birthday.

examples.tl: Hindi ako kuripot, matipid lang.
examples.en: I'm not cheap, just thrifty.

notes: Spanish loan. Someone who always picks up the tab. 'Mapagbigay' = generous (formal).

examples.tl: Galante si Tito Jun, siya ang nagbayad ng buong dinner.
examples.en: Uncle Jun is generous, he paid for the whole dinner.

notes: Root galang (respect). Using po/opo and mano makes you 'magalang'. Top compliment for a partner meeting the family.

examples.tl: Magalang ang jowa ni ate, laging po at opo.
examples.en: Big sister's boyfriend is respectful, always po and opo.

examples.tl: Magalang ang mga bata nila.
examples.en: Their kids are polite.

notes: Strong. Rude manners or vulgar jokes/behavior. 'Ang bastos!' = how rude! 'Walang galang' = no respect.

examples.tl: Bastos ang lalaki sa jeep, sinisiksik ang mga babae.
examples.en: The guy on the jeep was rude, crowding the women.

examples.tl: Bastos ang joke niya sa harap ng mga bata.
examples.en: His joke was vulgar in front of the kids.

notes: Chismosa (f) / chismoso (m). 'Chismis' = gossip (noun). 'Mag-chismis tayo' = let's catch up on gossip. Playful among friends.

examples.tl: Chismosa ang kapitbahay namin, alam niya lahat.
examples.en: Our neighbor is a gossip, she knows everything.

examples.tl: Chismoso ang GC ng barkada, may update araw-araw.
examples.en: The barkada group chat is gossipy, there's an update every day.

notes: As in English, for partners and gestures. 'Sweet niyo!' = you two are so sweet. Tagalog: malambing.

examples.tl: Sweet ng jowa mo, hinatid ka hanggang condo.
examples.en: Your partner is sweet, took you all the way to the condo.

examples.tl: Ang sweet ng message ni Lola sa GC.
examples.en: Grandma's message in the group chat was so sweet.

notes: Said 'kay-jay'. The friend who won't join or shuts down the fun. 'Huwag kang KJ!' = don't be a buzzkill.

examples.tl: Huwag kang KJ, sumama ka sa inuman.
examples.en: Don't be a killjoy, come to the drinking session.

notes: Maki(pag)- = join in doing with others. 'Nakipag-usap ako sa landlord' = I talked with the landlord. Casual 'usap tayo' = let's talk.

examples.tl: Gusto kong makipag-usap sa admin ng condo tungkol sa parking.
examples.en: I want to talk with the condo admin about parking.

examples.tl: Usap tayo mamaya, may sasabihin ako.
examples.en: Let's talk later, I have something to tell you.

notes: Object focus: kinausap (talked to), kinakausap (is talking to), kakausapin (will talk to). 'Kausapin mo siya' = talk to her.

examples.tl: Kinausap ko na si boss tungkol sa leave ko.
examples.en: I already talked to the boss about my leave.

examples.tl: Kausapin mo ang kapatid mo, nagtatampo siya.
examples.en: Talk to your brother, he's sulking.

notes: Tinawagan (called), tinatawagan (is calling), tatawagan (will call). 'Tawagan mo ako' = call me. 'Tumawag' = to make a call.

examples.tl: Tawagan mo si Mama, nag-aalala siya.
examples.en: Call Mom, she's worried.

examples.tl: Tinawagan ako ng Grab driver, hindi niya mahanap ang gate.
examples.en: The Grab driver called me, he couldn't find the gate.

notes: Taglish: i-text (to text), nag-text (texted), tine-text (is texting), 'text mo ako' = text me. Also 'mag-text'.

examples.tl: I-text mo ako kapag nakauwi ka na.
examples.en: Text me when you get home.

examples.tl: Nag-text si Tita, pupunta daw siya sa Sabado.
examples.en: Auntie texted, she says she's coming on Saturday.

notes: Messenger/Viber/WhatsApp messages are 'chat', not 'text'. 'I-chat mo ako', 'nag-chat siya', 'chat lang kita'. 'GC' = group chat.

examples.tl: I-chat mo lang ako sa Messenger, wala akong load.
examples.en: Just message me on Messenger, I have no load.

examples.tl: Nag-chat ang ex ko kagabi. Hindi ko pa nire-reply.
examples.en: My ex messaged last night. I haven't replied yet.

notes: Every barkada, family and office has one (Messenger/Viber). 'Nasa GC' = it's in the group chat. 'Nag-mute ako ng GC' = I muted the GC.

examples.tl: Nasa GC ng pamilya ang details ng reunion.
examples.en: The reunion details are in the family group chat.

examples.tl: Ang ingay ng GC ng barkada kagabi, 200 messages.
examples.en: The barkada group chat was so noisy last night, 200 messages.

notes: Reciprocal (two or more people). Nag-away (fought), nag-aaway (fighting), mag-aaway (will fight). 'Away' = a fight. 'LQ' = lovers' quarrel.

examples.tl: Nag-away kami ng jowa ko kagabi, LQ lang.
examples.en: My partner and I fought last night, just a lovers' quarrel.

examples.tl: Lagi silang nag-aaway tungkol sa pera.
examples.en: They always fight about money.

notes: 'Kami' excludes the listener. 'Nag-away kami ni Mama' = Mom and I fought. 'Nag-usap na kami' usually follows when it's resolved.

examples.tl: Nag-away kami ni kuya dahil sa utang.
examples.en: My brother and I had a fight over a debt.

examples.tl: Nag-away kami pero okay na ulit kami.
examples.en: We fought but we're okay again.

notes: 'Bati na kami' = we're on good terms again (very common). 'Hindi sila nagbabati' = they're not speaking. Root bati = greet / be on terms.

examples.tl: Nagkabati na kami ng ate ko after two weeks.
examples.en: My sister and I made up after two weeks.

examples.tl: Bati na ba kayo ng jowa mo?
examples.en: Are you and your partner good again?

notes: Taglish, the everyday verb. Nag-sorry (apologized), 'mag-sorry ka' = say sorry. 'Sorry na' = come on, I'm sorry. Formal: humingi ng tawad.

examples.tl: Nag-sorry na ako, ano pa ba ang gusto mo?
examples.en: I already said sorry, what else do you want?

examples.tl: Mag-sorry ka kay Lola, nasaktan siya.
examples.en: Apologize to Grandma, she was hurt.

notes: More serious/sincere than mag-sorry. 'Patawad' = forgive me / forgiveness. 'Patawarin mo ako' = forgive me.

examples.tl: Humingi siya ng tawad sa mga magulang niya.
examples.en: He asked his parents for forgiveness.

examples.tl: Patawad, hindi ko sinasadya.
examples.en: Forgive me, I didn't mean it.

notes: Nagpasalamat (thanked). Everyday thanks is just 'salamat' / 'thank you'. 'Pasasalamat' = gratitude; 'thanksgiving party' is common after a blessing.

examples.tl: Nagpasalamat ako sa mga tumulong noong bagyo.
examples.en: I thanked those who helped during the typhoon.

examples.tl: Magpasalamat ka kay Tita, siya ang nagbayad ng tuition mo.
examples.en: Thank Auntie, she's the one who paid your tuition.

notes: Binati (greeted), binabati (is greeting). 'Batiin mo si Tito' = say hi to Uncle. Also 'congratulate' and 'greet on a birthday'. 'Bati' = a greeting.

examples.tl: Batiin mo si Lola, birthday niya ngayon.
examples.en: Greet Grandma, it's her birthday today.

examples.tl: Hindi niya ako binati sa hallway, suplado.
examples.en: He didn't greet me in the hallway, snob.

notes: Verbs: yumakap (to hug, actor), yakapin (to hug someone), nagyakapan (hugged each other). Text: 'yakap!' or 'virtual hug'.

examples.tl: Yakap muna bago umalis.
examples.en: Hug first before leaving.

examples.tl: Niyakap ako ni Mama sa airport, umiyak pa.
examples.en: Mom hugged me at the airport, even cried.

notes: Often implies a serious talk ('nag-usap kami nang masinsinan'). 'Nag-usap na kami' = we've talked it out. 'Mag-usap tayo' = let's talk.

examples.tl: Nag-usap kami ng jowa ko tungkol sa future namin.
examples.en: My partner and I talked about our future.

examples.tl: Nag-usap na kami ni kuya, okay na.
examples.en: My brother and I already talked, it's fine now.

notes: 'Kilala' = know a person (vs 'alam' = know a fact). 'Kilala mo ba siya?' = do you know her? 'Hindi ko siya kilala' = I don't know him.

examples.tl: Kilala ko siya, kaklase ko sa high school.
examples.en: I know her, she was my high school classmate.

examples.tl: Kilala mo ba 'yung bagong tenant sa 12th floor?
examples.en: Do you know the new tenant on the 12th floor?

notes: From makilala. 'Nakilala ko siya sa...' = I met her at... 'Makilala' = to meet/get to know. Not for appointments (that's magkita).

examples.tl: Nakilala ko ang jowa ko sa gym sa Makati.
examples.en: I met my partner at a gym in Makati.

examples.tl: Gusto kong makilala ang pamilya mo.
examples.en: I want to meet your family.

notes: Ipinakilala (introduced). 'Ipakilala mo ako' = introduce me. 'Magpakilala' = introduce yourself. 'Pakilala' = an introduction.

examples.tl: Ipakilala mo naman ako sa tita mo.
examples.en: Come on, introduce me to your aunt.

examples.tl: Ipinakilala niya ako sa parents niya noong Pasko.
examples.en: He introduced me to his parents at Christmas.

notes: Reciprocal. 'Kita tayo' = let's meet. 'Nagkita kami' = we met up. 'Kita-kits' = see you (slang). 'Mag-meet' also common.

examples.tl: Kita tayo sa Greenbelt mamaya, 7 PM.
examples.en: Let's meet at Greenbelt later, 7 PM.

examples.tl: Nagkita kami ng barkada ko sa Poblacion.
examples.en: My friends and I met up in Poblacion.

notes: Nag-date (went on a date), 'ka-date' = your date. 'Date night', 'dinner date' as-is. 'Nililigawan' = being courted.

examples.tl: Nag-date kami sa Salcedo market noong Sabado.
examples.en: We went on a date at the Salcedo market on Saturday.

examples.tl: Sino ang ka-date mo sa Valentine's?
examples.en: Who's your date on Valentine's?

notes: Nanligaw (courted), nanliligaw (is courting). 'Ligaw' = courtship; 'manliligaw' = suitor; 'ligawan' = to court someone. Still a real stage before 'official'.

examples.tl: Nanligaw siya sa akin nang isang taon bago kami naging official.
examples.en: He courted me for a year before we became official.

examples.tl: May nanliligaw kay ate, officemate niya.
examples.en: Someone's courting big sister, her officemate.

notes: The traditional stage: 'ligaw stage', 'nililigawan' (being courted). 'Sinagot' = she said yes (literally: answered).

examples.tl: Nasa ligaw stage pa sila, hindi pa sila.
examples.en: They're still in the courtship stage, not official yet.

examples.tl: Sinagot na niya ang nanliligaw sa kanya.
examples.en: She finally said yes to her suitor.

notes: 'Crush ko siya' = I have a crush on him. 'May crush ako sa 'yo' = I have a crush on you. 'Crush ng bayan' = everyone's crush. 'Crush kita' is a confession.

examples.tl: Crush ko ang barista sa Salcedo, HAHAHA.
examples.en: I have a crush on the barista in Salcedo, haha.

examples.tl: Crush ng bayan ang bagong officemate.
examples.en: The new officemate is everyone's crush.

notes: Nag-break (broke up), 'break na sila' = they're done. 'Nakipag-break' = broke up with someone. 'Hiwalay' = separated (also for married couples).

examples.tl: Nag-break sila after five years, nakakalungkot.
examples.en: They broke up after five years, it's sad.

examples.tl: Break na sila ng jowa niya, kaya bitter.
examples.en: She and her partner broke up, that's why she's bitter.

notes: Root amin. 'Umamin siya sa crush niya' = he confessed to his crush. 'Aminin mo!' = admit it! 'Nag-confess' also common.

examples.tl: Umamin siya sa akin na may gusto siya sa akin.
examples.en: He confessed to me that he has feelings for me.

examples.tl: Aminin mo, crush mo siya!
examples.en: Admit it, you have a crush on her!

notes: From 'standby'. 'Tambay' = hanging out / an idle person; 'tambayan' = hangout spot. 'Tambay tayo' = let's chill.

examples.tl: Tumambay kami sa condo ko, nag-Netflix lang.
examples.en: We hung out at my condo, just watched Netflix.

examples.tl: Tambay tayo sa coffee shop after work.
examples.en: Let's hang out at the coffee shop after work.

notes: The barkada's main event. 'Mag-inuman' = to have drinks. 'Inom tayo' = let's drink. 'Pulutan' = bar food.

examples.tl: May inuman sa bahay ni Jake sa Friday, sama ka?
examples.en: There's a drinking session at Jake's on Friday, you coming?

examples.tl: Nag-inuman kami hanggang 3 AM, hangover ako ngayon.
examples.en: We drank until 3 AM, I'm hungover now.

notes: Dumalaw (visited), dadalaw (will visit). 'Dalawin' = visit someone (object focus). 'Bumisita' is the synonym. Visiting the sick/elderly is a strong norm.

examples.tl: Dadalaw kami kay Lola sa ospital mamaya.
examples.en: We're visiting Grandma at the hospital later.

examples.tl: Dalawin mo naman ang parents mo, matagal ka nang hindi umuuwi.
examples.en: Visit your parents, you haven't gone home in a long time.

notes: 'Ano ang chismis?' = what's the tea? 'Mag-chismis' / 'mag-chismisan' = to gossip. 'Marites' = a gossipy person (meme).

examples.tl: Ano ang latest chismis sa office?
examples.en: What's the latest gossip at the office?

examples.tl: Chismis lang 'yan, hindi totoo.
examples.en: That's just a rumor, it's not true.

notes: Two uses: 'asar ako' = I'm irritated; 'inaasar niya ako' = he's teasing me. 'Asaran' = mutual teasing (barkada love language). 'Asar talo' = sore loser.

examples.tl: Lagi akong inaasar ng barkada ko tungkol sa crush ko.
examples.en: My friends always tease me about my crush.

examples.tl: Asar ako, nakalimutan ko ulit ang password ko.
examples.en: I'm irritated, I forgot my password again.

notes: Messenger culture: 'Na-seen lang ako' = he saw it and didn't reply. 'Seen-zoned ako'. The source of much praning.

examples.tl: Na-seen lang ako ng crush ko. Sad.
examples.en: My crush just left me on read. Sad.

examples.tl: Huwag mo akong i-seen-zone, reply ka naman.
examples.en: Don't leave me on read, reply, come on.

notes: Formal-ish; people mostly say 'birthday'. 'Maligayang kaarawan' = happy birthday (on cards). The celebrant treats everyone ('libre').

examples.tl: Kaarawan ni Mama sa Linggo, handaan sa bahay.
examples.en: It's Mom's birthday on Sunday, a party at the house.

examples.tl: Happy birthday, bes! Libre mo mamaya ha.
examples.en: Happy birthday, bestie! Your treat later, okay.

notes: Reverse of the US custom: the celebrant pays. 'Pa-birthday mo!' = treat us for your birthday! 'Pa-blowout' is the older term.

examples.tl: Pa-birthday mo naman, boss!
examples.en: Treat us for your birthday, boss!

examples.tl: Pizza ang pa-birthday niya sa office.
examples.en: Her birthday treat for the office was pizza.

notes: 'Kasal na sila' = they're married. 'Ikakasal' = getting married. 'Kasalan' = the wedding event. 'Ninong/ninang sa kasal' = wedding sponsors.

examples.tl: Kasal ng pinsan ko sa Tagaytay sa December.
examples.en: My cousin's wedding is in Tagaytay in December.

examples.tl: Ikakasal na si ate next year!
examples.en: Big sister is getting married next year!

notes: Nagpakasal (got married), magpapakasal (will get married). 'Nag-propose' / 'engaged' as-is. Civil wedding = 'civil', church = 'church wedding'.

examples.tl: Nagpakasal sila sa civil muna, church wedding next year.
examples.en: They had a civil wedding first, church wedding next year.

examples.tl: Kailan kayo magpapakasal?
examples.en: When are you two getting married?

notes: Big family event with many ninongs/ninangs. 'Bibinyagan' = will be baptized. Followed by a handaan.

examples.tl: Binyag ng anak ni kuya sa Sabado, ninong ako.
examples.en: My brother's kid's baptism is Saturday, I'm the godfather.

examples.tl: Puro bisita sa bahay after ng binyag.
examples.en: The house was full of guests after the christening.

notes: From mamatay. 'Namatay na ang lolo ko' = my grandpa has passed. Softer: 'pumanaw', 'wala na' (is gone). 'Patay' = dead.

examples.tl: Namatay ang lola niya kagabi, kaya absent siya.
examples.en: Her grandmother died last night, so she's absent.

examples.tl: Wala na si Lolo, pero lagi ko siyang naaalala.
examples.en: Grandpa is gone, but I always remember him.

notes: Multi-day wake, often at home or a funeral chapel, with food, coffee and card games. Showing up matters more than words. 'Makiramay' = to condole.

examples.tl: Pupunta ako sa lamay ng tatay ng officemate ko mamaya.
examples.en: I'm going to the wake of my officemate's dad later.

examples.tl: Three days ang lamay, tapos libing sa Sabado.
examples.en: The wake is three days, then the burial on Saturday.

notes: 'Ililibing' = will be buried. 'Punerarya' = funeral home. People say 'funeral' too. Wear black or white.

examples.tl: Umuwi siya sa probinsya para sa libing ng lola niya.
examples.en: He went home to the province for his grandmother's funeral.

examples.tl: Sa Loyola Marikina ang libing.
examples.en: The burial is at Loyola Marikina.

notes: 'Condolence' (singular) is what people actually text, plus 'praying for your family'. Tagalog: 'Nakikiramay ako/kami' (I/we share your grief).

examples.tl: Condolence sa inyo, pare. Nandito lang kami.
examples.en: Condolences to you all, bro. We're here for you.

examples.tl: Nakikiramay kami sa pamilya ni Tita Nena.
examples.en: We offer our condolences to Auntie Nena's family.

notes: As-is. 'Nag-graduate' = graduated. 'Pagtatapos' is the formal word on programs. Whole family attends, then a celebratory lunch.

examples.tl: Graduation ng pamangkin ko sa UST sa June.
examples.en: My niece's graduation at UST is in June.

examples.tl: Nag-graduate na ang bunso, buong pamilya nag-Jollibee.
examples.en: The youngest graduated, the whole family went to Jollibee.

notes: Taglish. 'Promotion' as-is. 'Na-regular' = became a regular employee (big deal after probation). Celebrant treats ('libre').

examples.tl: Na-promote si ate, team lead na siya!
examples.en: Big sister got promoted, she's a team lead now!

examples.tl: Libre mo, na-promote ka!
examples.en: Your treat, you got promoted!

notes: People say 'anniversary' or 'anniv'. 'Monthsary' = monthly anniversary (young couples, taken seriously).

examples.tl: Anniversary ng parents ko sa Sabado, 30 years.
examples.en: My parents' anniversary is Saturday, 30 years.

examples.tl: Nakalimutan niya ang monthsary namin, nagtatampo ako.
examples.en: He forgot our monthsary, I'm sulking.

notes: Every barangay/town has one. Open houses, everyone eats everywhere, 'kain lang'. Famous ones: Sinulog, Ati-Atihan, Pahiyas.

examples.tl: Fiesta sa barangay nila sa Mayo, inimbita ako.
examples.en: Their barangay fiesta is in May, I was invited.

examples.tl: Sa fiesta, puwede kang kumain sa kahit anong bahay.
examples.en: At the fiesta, you can eat at any house.

notes: Season starts in September ('ber months'). 'Maligayang Pasko' = Merry Christmas. 'Aguinaldo' = cash gift from ninongs; 'Noche Buena' = Christmas Eve feast.

examples.tl: Uuwi ako sa probinsya sa Pasko.
examples.en: I'm going home to the province for Christmas.

examples.tl: Maligayang Pasko sa inyong lahat!
examples.en: Merry Christmas to all of you!

notes: 'Manigong Bagong Taon' = Happy New Year. 'Media Noche' = midnight feast; round fruits, polka dots, loud noise for luck.

examples.tl: Saan kayo mag-Bagong Taon? Sa amin ka na lang.
examples.en: Where are you spending New Year's? Just come to ours.

examples.tl: Manigong Bagong Taon, Tita! Ingat po kayo.
examples.en: Happy New Year, Auntie! Take care.

notes: Families go to the cemetery, clean graves, light candles, eat. Heavy traffic out of Manila. 'Araw ng mga Patay' is the formal name.

examples.tl: Uuwi kami sa Bulacan sa Undas para dalawin si Lolo.
examples.en: We're going home to Bulacan for Undas to visit Grandpa's grave.

examples.tl: Traffic sa NLEX tuwing Undas.
examples.en: NLEX is jammed every Undas.

notes: Manila empties out; Maundy Thursday and Good Friday are holidays, malls close. Visita Iglesia (church visits), 'Mahal na Araw' in Tagalog.

examples.tl: Tahimik ang Makati tuwing Holy Week, lahat umuuwi sa probinsya.
examples.en: Makati is quiet every Holy Week, everyone goes home to the province.

examples.tl: Bawal mag-ingay sa bahay ni Lola sa Good Friday.
examples.en: No noise allowed at Grandma's house on Good Friday.

notes: Root handa (to prepare). Any celebration with lots of food: birthday, binyag, fiesta. 'May handaan' = there's a party. Guests take home 'baon'.

examples.tl: May handaan sa bahay ni Tita sa Sabado, 50th birthday niya.
examples.en: There's a party at Auntie's house on Saturday, her 50th birthday.

examples.tl: Ang dami ng pagkain sa handaan, may lechon!
examples.en: So much food at the party, there was lechon!

notes: Spanish loan. Thrown for someone leaving (abroad, new job). Opposite: 'welcome party' or 'bienvenida' (rare).

examples.tl: Despedida ni Marco sa Friday, aalis siya papuntang Canada.
examples.en: Marco's farewell party is Friday, he's leaving for Canada.

examples.tl: Umiyak lahat sa despedida ni ate.
examples.en: Everyone cried at big sister's send-off.

notes: Pronounced 'de-BOO'. Formal party with 18 roses, 18 candles. Boys' 21st is less of a thing. 'Debutante' = the celebrant.

examples.tl: Debut ng pamangkin ko sa November, may 18 roses.
examples.en: My niece's debut is in November, with the 18 roses.

examples.tl: Kasama ako sa 18 roses sa debut niya.
examples.en: I'm one of the 18 roses at her debut.

notes: As-is. Family reunions at Christmas, batch reunions at homecoming. Expect 'tita questions' about weight and love life.

examples.tl: Family reunion sa Pasko, 60 tao sa bahay ni Lola.
examples.en: Family reunion at Christmas, 60 people at Grandma's house.

examples.tl: Hindi ako pupunta sa batch reunion, puro tanong kung may jowa na.
examples.en: I'm not going to the batch reunion, all questions about whether I have a partner.

notes: 'Buntis si ate' = sis is pregnant. 'Nabuntis' = got pregnant. 'Preggy' is the cute Taglish version. 'Nanganak' = gave birth.

examples.tl: Buntis na ang asawa ni kuya, due sa March.
examples.en: My brother's wife is pregnant, due in March.

examples.tl: Nanganak na si ate kagabi, baby girl!
examples.en: Big sister gave birth last night, a baby girl!

notes: Take an elder's hand and touch it to your forehead on arrival; they say 'God bless'. Expected at family gatherings. 'Magmano' = do the mano.

examples.tl: Mano po, Lola. Kumusta po kayo?
examples.en: Bless, Grandma. How are you?

examples.tl: Magmano ka kay Tito bago kumain.
examples.en: Do the mano to Uncle before eating.
